question.text: The Sponsor of the Himalaya Arbitrage Fund is evaluating whether to domicile the fund onshore in India or via an offshore feeder. Which service provider is MOST appropriate to advise on this structuring decision?

answer.text: Merchant Banker — because they file the PPM.
Custodian — because they handle the securities settlement.
Tax Advisor — because fund domicile decisions are driven by tax-efficiency and cross-border considerations.
RTA — because they issue and transfer units.

explanation.text: The Logic: Tax Advisors are specifically appointed by AIF managers for advice on fund domicile, offshore vs onshore structuring, pre/post-tax NAV, advance-tax estimation, TDS treatment, and cross-border tax compliance — including GIFT-IFSC benefits under Section 80LA. Offshore tax-friendly jurisdictions help avoid cascading taxation. Merchant bankers, custodians, and RTAs serve different functional purposes. The Trap: The trap is assuming any adviser-style provider (MB, custodian) can substitute for a tax adviser. Fund domicile is inherently a tax-structuring decision. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XIX-D test the same role. XXI-B (PM) has tax considerations but simpler (no fund-domicile choice). IA/RA exams (X-A, XV) test tax concepts at entity level.
